content.user_title: Verify Research and Facts for Authors
content.value_statement: Authors often need accurate details without slowing the writing process. This skill creates research plans, fact-check reports, and source tracking workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates structured research briefs for story topics and settings.
Extracts factual claims from manuscript passages for review.
Flags inaccuracies, anachronisms, and unverifiable claims.
Suggests source categories, expert consultations, and cross-check steps.
Builds bibliography templates for tracking research evidence.
Shows ways to integrate facts into scenes without info dumps.
limitations: It cannot guarantee accuracy without credible sources or browsing support.
It does not replace historians, scientists, cultural consultants, or editors.
It needs clear genre, setting, time period, and accuracy goals.
It focuses on writing research, not legal, medical, or financial advice.

use_cases.title: Plan Historical Research
use_cases.description: Build a focused research brief for a time period, location, profession, or cultural setting.

use_cases.title: Check Scientific Plausibility
use_cases.description: Review a speculative scene for physical limits, technical assumptions, and reader-facing credibility.

use_cases.title: Verify Nonfiction Claims
use_cases.description: Identify factual claims, assign verification status, and suggest stronger source support.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Research Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am writing [genre] about [topic]. Create a research brief with key questions, source types, red flags, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Fact-Check a Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Fact-check this passage for [time period or domain]. List accurate claims, inaccurate claims, unverifiable claims, and suggested revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Source System
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bibliography and note-taking structure for my book about [subject]. Include reliability ratings and story relevance fields.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Accuracy Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this chapter for accuracy risks. Prioritize issues by reader impact, source confidence, revision effort, and expert review needs.

output_examples.input: A novelist asks what to research for an American art student in 1920s Paris.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a brief covering art schools, housing, money, transport, social norms, source types, myths, and cross-check tasks.

output_examples.input: A writer submits a Mars colony paragraph with breathable air and normal outdoor walking.
output_examples.output: The skill flags atmospheric pressure, temperature, radiation, and apparent Earth size issues, then suggests plausible scene revisions.

output_examples.input: An editor needs a repeatable process for tracking research across chapters.
output_examples.output: The skill provides bibliography sections, expert consultation notes, source reliability labels, and follow-up research tasks.

best_practices: Provide genre, time period, location, and desired accuracy level before asking for research.
Ask for source reliability notes and independent cross-checks on important claims.
Use the suggested revisions as starting points, then verify facts with current sources.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated research notes as final evidence without checking sources.
Do not ask for broad research when a focused claim or scene needs review.
Do not use factual detail only to display research if it does not serve the story.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the web?
faq.answer: The skill provides research structure and verification methods. Actual browsing depends on the host tool and available permissions.

faq.question: Can it verify historical facts?
faq.answer: It can identify claims, suggest source types, and flag likely anachronisms. Final verification still needs credible sources.

faq.question: Is it useful for science fiction?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps check scientific plausibility, explain constraints, and propose believable alternatives for speculative scenes.

faq.question: Can it help with cultural accuracy?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends first-person sources, cultural consultants, and sensitivity review when cultural details matter.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the passage, setting, time period, genre, target audience, and the level of realism you want.

faq.question: Does it replace expert review?
faq.answer: No. It helps prepare focused questions and notes, but expert review is still important for specialized topics.
